key_insight: A temporal machine learning time-to-event model can combine longitudinal ALSFRS-R data with survival analysis to predict individualized functional decline and wheelchair-free survival in ALS.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help clinicians anticipate progression, support proactive care planning, and identify patients for earlier intervention or trial stratification.
method: Harmonized longitudinal ALS data from diagnosis, ALSFRS-R, activities of daily living, and demographics
Used correlation-based clustering and generalized additive mixed models to map domain-specific decline
Built a temporal ML + Cox time-to-event framework to generate individualized survival curves
evidence_signal: The abstract describes development on a harmonized longitudinal cohort with temporal alignment and cohort consistency checks, but does not report performance metrics in the abstract.
watch_item: Because the abstract does not provide external validation or calibration results, real-world generalizability and implementation reliability still need confirmation.
paper_title: A Temporal Machine Learning-Based Time-to-Event Model for Predicting ALS Progression and Healthcare Utilization
